items.title: Lawrence Douglas Harris Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...most of the piano players, they didn't read. You take in New Orleans, Paul, there were a number of piano players...

ctx.x: Incidentally I see where she gotta write up where she stuff Yeah, she cut out and cut some records again. I'd like to hear that. I played for her. And that little boy out of Houston, I don't know if you remember him, dog, my name was Skinny, he couldn't read but he could play the best piano player ever in my life. He was really terrific.

Well it seemed in those days, I'll say from the early 20s to the first to the 30s, most of the piano players, they didn't read. You take in New Orleans, Paul, there were a number of piano players while they couldn't read but played so terrific piano.
And the chords were perfect. You can check them today and the chords were right, it was great.
